column1: # Seconds per suite on GitHub's 2-core Linux machine, read from the suite tables in the parts' logs (15 Nov, P-436 (7),
# P-502): the median of the PASS rows of the 8 newest green merge-queue batch runs with 8 parts (43656353002,
# timed there, 1-8 samples each). Suites those batches skipped (on CI's automatic quarantine, B122) take their one PASS
# row in the finished parts 1-7 of scheduled nightly run 43655888932 (15 Nov, 13 suites). The 5 on run-suites.sh's
# hand-set QUARANTINE list, which only the nightly runs, take the median of their nightly PASS rows of 6-11 Nov (runs
# 1230 s, its measured hang (it passes in 0-1 s, but twice ran into the 1200 s suite limit + 30 s kill, runs
# 42243001915 and 42377102612; see QUARANTINE). Its nightly part is dealt that time, so the part still ends inside the
# job limit when it hangs. Set it back to its pass time (0) when it leaves the quarantine.
# Nightly suites ran at 0.98 x these medians (356 suites in both); one part's sum ran 0.74-1.23 x them (71 parts).
# run-suites.sh --shard balances the shards by these times (longest first); a suite missing here counts as 30 s; a
# quarantined suite weighs 0 only where it is skipped (PR and queue checks), its time in the nightly full set.
# Refresh the same way when many suites are new (15 Nov: 15 suites were untimed, 30 s each, and nightly part 8 stopped
# at its 59-minute limit twice; earlier: 14 Nov file, 7ca355ba7).
